justification_text:
The point estimates in this forecast are based on a projection of the most likely value at each time horizon, given current trends, historical patterns, and known factors influencing the variable in question. For all three time frames—1 day, 1 week, and 1 month—the point estimate is the same at 149.11. This indicates that we are assuming the near-term value will remain stable, likely because there is no strong directional signal suggesting a sharp rise or fall. It could also reflect the belief that while small fluctuations might occur, they are insufficient to deviate meaningfully from the current level in the short term.

The confidence interval (CI), which widens as the time horizon increases from 1 day to 1 week to 1 month, reflects growing uncertainty over longer periods. In the short term, fewer uncertainties are likely to accumulate, so the range of possible outcomes remains tighter (e.g., 90% of outcomes falling within [147.62, 150.6] over 1 day). However, as more time passes, there is more room for unexpected events, randomness, or changing trends to come into play, which is why the 1-week and 1-month intervals grow progressively wider. Factors contributing to this uncertainty might include market volatility, shifts in external conditions (like economic data or geopolitical developments), or the underlying noise typically present in any real-world system.

There are always risks or events that could push outcomes outside the stated intervals. For example, unexpected news—such as major policy announcements, sharp shifts in macroeconomic indicators, or surprise earnings results—could drive the variable far above or below the predicted range. Over the 1-month horizon, structural changes, new risks, or even a broad market correction could significantly alter the trend. Such risks reflect the "fat tails" often seen in real-world distributions, where rare but extreme events can have outsized impacts. While the model accounts for typical uncertainty and variability, it may not fully capture the likelihood of these rare, high-impact events.
